sentences.text:
This is first bail application under Section 439 of the Cr.P.C. filed by the applicant for grant of regular bail in relation to FIR No.190/2019 dated 18.07.2019 registered at Police Station Orchha,
Niwari for commission of offence under Sections 420, 467, 468 and 406 of IPC.

Applicant is in detention since 03.11.2023.
2.
As per the prosecution story, applicant was arrested in relation to FIR No.190/2019 of Police Station Orchha, Niwari for commission of offence under Sections 420, 467, 468 and 406 of IPC.
He was released on bail and was facing sessions trial.
It is alleged that he failed to appear before the trial Court on 09.03.2021 and 23.10.2021.
Consequently, his application under Section 317 of Cr.P.C. was dismissed and arrest warrant was issued to procure his appearance.

Thereafter,
perpetual arrest warrant was issued.
However, on 03.11.2023, applicant himself surrendered before the trial Court and since then he is in jail.

1 3.
Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that applicant was on bail.

He had instructed his Advocate to inform him about the dates when he has to appear before the trial Court but his Advocate never informed him about the dates on which he had to appear before the trial Court.
On 09.03.2021 witnesses Rakesh Kewat and on 22.10.2021 Dayachand Ahirwar turned up in the Court but they could not be cross-
examined as accused was not present.
After surrender, his bail application has been dismissed and he is in jail for the last more than two months.
He will not repeat such mistake in future.
Therefore, it is prayed that one more opportunity may be given to him to remain on bail.
4 . On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent/State has opposed grant of bail to the applicant.

5. In this case, witness Rakesh Kewat has already been examined and cross- examined, whereas it is informed that Dayachand (PW/2) is no more and an intelligible copy of his death certificate has been filed.

Undoubtedly, the trial has been delayed due to absence of the accused but at the same time it cannot be overlooked that the applicant is facing trial since 2019 and final conclusion of the trial will still take considerable time.

Therefore, I am of the view that it would be just and proper to grant him one more opportunity to remain on bail by imposing stringent conditions as he has learnt sufficient lesson for his absence from the trial Court.
Consequently, this bail application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure filed on behalf of applicant, stands allowed.

6 . I t is directed that applicant - Ansar Raza be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it till the final outcome of case.
He shall not seek adjournments whenever witnesses are in attendance.

He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C.
7.
Learned trial Court shall be at liberty to proceed under Section 446 of Cr.P.C. against applicant and his surety to levy the penalty.
8. This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.
